name: Erba murder bible cryptogram (2013 encrypted message hidden in a bible by Olindo Romano)
date: message content dated by Schmeh to '2013 press reports'; the murders themselves were December 2006
ciphertext: Image re-transcribed 25 Sept 2026 (LANE B3 bERB, cheap test 1) from ciphers/erba-2006/images/Erba-Cryptogram.png, checked against comment #3's community reading (reader 'Marc', 16 Aug 2017): 93.0% digraph-identity agreement over 114 tokens (specs/cheap-tests/erba-2006/diff_output.txt), all 8 disagreements the same 'me' vs 'ne' pair at 8 of the 114 positions -- a real handwriting ambiguity (cursive m/n before e), not settled either way, grade M. bERB's own reading, natural page order, plaintext lead-in excluded: 'cu Mi / xs fi un Ro fi cu me un xs Pi cu Ro me cu / mi xs mi (Bild) NE un cu Ro / fi Ro un (Bild) fi Mi xs me / xs me cu fi (Bild) un cu mi Ro / ne Mi un (Bild) me mi xs Pi / Ro mi Pi (Bild) un mi Ro cu / cu ne Ro- (Bild) xs cu ne cu Pi / Cu mi fi un Ro ne cu xs Pi Ne un Mi fi NE / ne un xs fi cu ne un mi fi cu Ro fi xs / Ne Ro fi cu xs fi Ro mi' plus two side blocks (both highlighted yellow in the image, beside the child illustration and the glued-in 'Amare' magazine clipping, both confirmed non-cipher by eye): 'Block right: cu xs fi mi cu / un Ro me xs / mi fi cu -' and 'Block left: un cu xs / Ro me fi me -'. Plaintext lead-in (not cipher, Italian, confirmed legible in the image): 'Pochi giorni prima - Poi'. Marc's original reading (comment #3, kept for the record, not deleted) is unchanged below in ciphertext_source; the two differ only in the me/ne positions and one case slip (Ro/ro). '(Bild)' marks a picture/illustration break in the bible page, not a ciphertext token.

Marc's comment #3 (16 Aug 2017), which itself corrects an initial 8-digraph count from comment #2 to 14 (case-sensitive: cu/Cu, mi/Mi, xs, fi, un, ro/Ro, ne/NE/Ne, pi/Pi), AS POSTED: '(Pochi ... - Poi) cu Mi / xs fi un ro fi cu ne un xs Pi cu Ro ne cu / mi xs mi (Bild) NE un cu Ro / fi Ro un (Bild) fi Mi xs ne / xs ne cu fi (Bild) un cu mi Ro / ne Mi un (Bild) ne mi xs Pi / Ro mi Pi (Bild) un mi Ro cu / cu ne Ro-(Bild) xs cu ne cu Pi / Cu mi fi un Ro ne cu xs Pi Ne un Mi fi NE / ne un xs fi cu ne un mi fi cu Ro fi xs / Ne Ro fi cu xs fi Ro mi' plus 'Block rechts: cu xs fi mi cu / un Ro ne xs / mi fi cu -' and 'Block links: un cu xs / Ro ne fi ne -'. Image over transcription (rule 2) is now satisfied for this field -- the primary `ciphertext` field above is from the image itself, not third-hand; Marc's reading (also from the same photograph, one step further removed) survives only as a cross-check, kept here for the record per rule 2 (never silently repaired).
alphabet: digraphs, not single letters: at least 8 base tokens (cu, mi, xs, fi, un, ro, ne, pi), each appearing in up to 3 case variants (lowercase, capitalized, all-caps) -- 14 distinct case-sensitive tokens on the commenter's count. UNRESOLVED as of 25 Sept 2026 (LANE B3 bERB, cheap test 1): 8 of 114 tokens read 'me' by this pass where the community transcription reads 'ne'; if any is correct as 'me' the true base alphabet is 9 tokens (adding 'me'), not 8, and K in cheap_tests_in_order[2] should be treated as 9-16ish pending resolution, not 8-14. Reader 'Dario' (quoted in the post body) hypothesises a syllable-substitution cipher ('alfabeto farfallino') where the ciphertext is designed to be pronounceable, and specifically guesses the unpronounceable digraph 'xs' marks word spacing.

constraints.context: Olindo Romano and his wife Rosa Bazzi murdered four neighbours in Erba, Italy, Dec 2006; a DIFFERENT, already-solved cryptogram (a pigpen-style MASC with nulls, deciphered without difficulty by police and used as trial evidence) is not this target -- Schmeh: 'I wish I could describe Orlindo Romano's encrypted messages here, but I have no access to them... Police had no trouble breaking it.' This spec is about the SECOND, still-unsolved 2013 message, found hidden in the Exodus chapter of an Italian bible Olindo sent his imprisoned wife.
constraints.hypothesised_cipher: reader Dario: probably a substitution cipher mapping single letters to syllables so the ciphertext reads as pronounceable (a variant of the historical 'alfabeto farfallino'); this is a source hypothesis, not established
constraints.content_hypothesis: Dario: the message likely concerns Romano's declared love for his wife, consistent with 2008 court statements that bible/paper notes ('pizzini') found on Romano contained love declarations, poems and insults against the victims and witnesses
constraints.possible_book_code_clue: commenter 'KunstundKetschup' (17 Aug 2017) speculates the opening digraph pair 'cu Mi' may encode a page number (81, via Exodus, since 'Poi' is read as referencing the book of Exodus) and a line 'NE.Micu.' between bible-text lines may encode a chapter:verse reference (21:18) -- explicitly speculative, offered with a shrug emoji, not a proposed decipherment
constraints.unencrypted_lead_in: the first words up to '- Poi' ('Pochi [giorni] ... - Poi', per reader Esme's later gloss 'a few days ago... and then') appear to be plaintext Italian, not part of the digraph cipher -- a plausible crib if confirmed against the image

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Fetch Erba-Bible.png and Erba-Cryptogram.png (scienceblogs.de) and independently re-transcribe the digraph sequence from the image, checking it against comment #3's reading above (case, digraph boundaries, and the '(Bild)'-marked picture breaks) before trusting a third-hand transcription for any test. Cost $2, Sonnet.

2. Once confirmed, test the 'xs = word space' hypothesis (reader Dario) by re-segmenting the sequence on xs and checking whether the resulting word-length profile (7 remaining digraphs -> Italian short-word plausibility) is more Italian-word-shaped than an unsegmented or randomly-segmented control of the same length. Cost $1.

3. With or without confirmed word breaks, a small-alphabet (8 base tokens, up to 14 with case) homophonic/syllable-substitution anneal against Italian, judged with a matched control (synthetic Italian syllable-substitution ciphertext at the same N and K, same solver); K=8-14 at this N is a favourable ratio compared to most items in this batch (CLAUDE.md rule 3: report both numbers). Cost $2-3.
matched_control: not yet run; test 3 above specifies the design (synthetic Italian syllable-substitution plaintext, same N/K, same solver)
